tasks.instruction: Run the video node once through the real RunningHub provider (Seedance image-to-video, route rhart-video/sparkvideo-2.0/image-to-video). The first frame must be the image artifact persisted by the earlier runninghub-seedream-t2i trial, exposed here as the declared artifact handle 'artifact_seedream_out' on the video node's first-frame reference: reuse it, do not regenerate the image and do not upload a new frame. Submit once, query to terminal SUCCESS, and leave exactly one persisted video artifact. The run is paid and pre-approved through the declared approval.

missingPredicates.name: provider.submit_references_include
missingPredicates.reason: The submit wire carries references (snapshot.providerLedger.submits[].wire.references) but no predicate reads it; only wire.mode is asserted via provider.mode_equals. 'First frame was the prior image artifact' is currently inferred from the node's metadata.references via reference.node_has_role, which is a proxy: it proves the node was configured with the reference, not that the submitted payload sent artifact_seedream_out as firstFrameUrl to RunningHub.

missingPredicates.name: artifact.persisted
missingPredicates.reason: Same gap as runninghub-seedream-t2i-001: no predicate asserts durable byte persistence; the RunningHub path never calls registerWorkflowArtifact today, so a driver that only sees artifact rows cannot distinguish a persisted video from a remote URL that expires in ~24h.

approvals: approve one real paid RunningHub Seedance image-to-video generation

tasks.runnerScopeReason: Real-provider certification: only a serial, parent-driven run against the live RunningHub API counts as evidence. Deterministic runners replay into the controlled world's fake provider, and the codex write-replay seam cannot express workflow.node.run, so these predicates grade only a driver that captures the real runtime/provider ledger into the normalized snapshot shape.
